batchName: Late Republic: Caesar's Civil War and the Ides of March (49-44 BCE) - Easy Batch 2
chapterName: Late Republic: Caesar's Civil War and the Ides of March (49-44 BCE)

questions.question: Near whose statue did Caesar fall after he was stabbed?
questions.explanation: He was killed in a hall in the Theatre of Pompey and fell near the statue of his old rival after 23 stab wounds.
questions.sourceQuote: Stabbed 23 times, he fell near Pompey's statue.

questions.question: Roughly how many men joined Brutus and his brother-in-law in the plot against Caesar?
questions.explanation: About sixty men joined the conspiracy, many of them Caesar's own officers.
questions.sourceQuote: About sixty men joined them, many of them Caesar's own officers.

questions.question: Which month was renamed in Caesar's honour?
questions.explanation: His birth month, Quinctilis, became July. The Senate also voted fifty days of thanksgiving and the title "Father of his Country".
questions.sourceQuote: A flattering Senate heaped on honours: fifty days of thanksgiving, the title "Father of his Country" (*parens patriae*), and the renaming of his birth month, Quinctilis, which became July.

questions.question: Near which place did the armies of Caesar and Pompey meet on 9 August 48 BC?
questions.explanation: The decisive battle took place near Pharsalus in Thessaly. By Caesar's own count he was outnumbered roughly two to one in infantry.
questions.sourceQuote: On 9 August 48 BC the armies met near Pharsalus.

questions.question: What office was Caesar granted early in 44 BC?
questions.explanation: Early in 44 BC Caesar was made dictator for life (dictator perpetuo), the climax of the honours heaped on him after Munda.
questions.sourceQuote: Early in 44 BC he was made dictator for life (*dictator perpetuo*).

questions.question: Which campaign did Caesar sum up with the words "I came, I saw, I conquered"?
questions.explanation: Caesar used the phrase in a letter about his brief campaign against the king of Pontus near Zela, where his men rallied while digging camp.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar summed up the brief campaign in a letter: "I came, I saw, I conquered" (*veni, vidi, vici*).

questions.question: What surprise did Caesar prepare to beat Pompey's cavalry charge at Pharsalus?
options: A reserve of war elephants on his left
A hidden fourth line of infantry behind his right
A cavalry ambush hidden in nearby woods
A trench lined with sharpened stakes
questions.explanation: When Pompey's horsemen charged, Caesar's hidden fourth line leapt up and jabbed javelins at them. The cavalry fled and Pompey's left wing collapsed.
questions.sourceQuote: But Caesar had hidden a fourth line behind his right.

questions.question: Who became Rome's first emperor in 27 BC?
questions.explanation: Caesar's will named his 18-year-old grandnephew as heir, and he took the Caesar name. In 27 BC he became Rome's first emperor.
questions.sourceQuote: In 27 BC the heir became Rome's first emperor.

questions.question: Whom did Caesar leave in charge of Italy when he marched to Spain in 49 BC?
questions.explanation: Caesar trusted his lieutenant Mark Antony with Italy while he marched west. In June he defeated Pompey's commanders at Ilerda.
questions.sourceQuote: Leaving Mark Antony, his trusted lieutenant, in charge of Italy, Caesar marched to Spain.

questions.question: On what date did the Ides of March fall?
questions.explanation: The Ides of March was 15 March, the date of the last Senate meeting before Caesar left to fight the Parthians.
questions.sourceQuote: The last one before he left to fight the Parthians, a great eastern empire, fell on the Ides of March (*Idus Martiae*), 15 March.
